title: Create E2e Saas
shortDescription: React + Vite This template provides a minimal setup to get React working in Vite with HMR and some ESLint rules. Currently, two official plugins are available: - @vitejs/plugin-rea...
description: The **create‑e2e‑saas** CLI scaffolds a full‑stack MERN application with a **React 19** client powered by Vite, a **Node.js**/Express backend, and **MongoDB** persistence. The generator copies a boilerplate template, sets up authentication flows, and wires together a secure, token‑based API using JWT, bcrypt, and Nodemailer for email verification. The architecture follows a **micro‑service‑like** pattern where the frontend and backend are decoupled yet tightly integrated through a well‑defined REST contract.
longDescription:
The project is bootstrapped via `npx create-e2e-saas <app-name>`, which triggers a Node.js CLI that copies the template files into the target directory using `fs-extra`. The CLI also installs dependencies and generates a `.env` file with placeholders for SMTP credentials and client URLs.

Once the scaffold is ready, the **frontend** is a Vite‑powered React 19 app that leverages Tailwind CSS for styling and Shadcn UI components for a consistent design system. Authentication state is managed through a global **Auth Context** that stores a JWT in an HTTP‑only cookie, ensuring protection against XSS. Routing is handled by **React Router 7**, with protected routes guarded by a custom hook that checks the authentication context.

The **backend** is an Express server exposing a set of REST endpoints under `/api/auth` and `/api/user`. Routes are defined in `authRoutes.js` and `userRoutes.js`, with middleware such as `userAuth` enforcing JWT validation. Controllers implement business logic: `register`, `login`, `logout`, `send-verify-otp`, `verify-account`, `send-reset-otp`, and `reset-password`. Passwords are hashed with **bcrypt**, and email verification is performed via **Nodemailer**.

Security guardrails include rate limiting on all auth endpoints, input validation with Joi, and sanitization to prevent injection attacks. Tokens are stored in HTTP‑only cookies, and the API uses CORS with a whitelist of the frontend origin. The build topology is split: the frontend is built with Vite into `frontend/dist`, while the backend is bundled with ES modules and run with `node --experimental-modules`.

Data ingestion flows from the frontend to the backend through Axios calls that include the JWT cookie. The backend validates the token, performs the requested action, and returns JSON responses. The database layer uses Mongoose schemas for users, with indexes on email and OTP fields to optimize lookups.

Section 1 System Topology: Engineered with JavaScript, combining a decoupled backend powered by Express and client interface built with React, TailwindCSS. Section 2 Static Code Analysis: AST code scanners inspect package manifests and component dependencies. Section 3 API Network Layer: Exposing 10 REST and WebSocket routes with parameter validation schemas. Section 4 Source Code Hierarchy: Codebase organized into isolated modules across Client, Src, Components, Pages. Section 5 Intelligence & Persistence: AI inference accelerated by Local ONNX Engine with persistence managed by MongoDB. Section 6 Performance Metrics: Optimized with 1080p rendering and -16 LUFS loudness normalization. Section 7 Deployment & Outro: Explore the complete repository on GitHub at Sameer-Bagul slash create-e2e-saas.
